newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican president's aide denies role in murder.
newsitem.headline: Mexican president's aide denies role in murder.

text.p: An aide to Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo denied in a letter published on Friday that he had any ties to the killers of a top politician.
Mexican newspaper Reforma said on Thursday that prosecutors were investigating Carlos Altamirano Toledo, director of administration at the President's Office, for supposed links to the assassination.
Altamirano, a former classmate of Zedillo and an Education Ministry official when Zedillo was minister, strongly denied any role in the killing in a letter published on Friday.

"All the assertions and suppositions that, according to your newspaper's story, Jorge Rodriguez Gonzalez made about me are false and absolutely baseless," Altamirano wrote. He did not mention whether he was under investigation.

Gonzalez is one of a pair of brothers accused of hiring the contract killer who gunned down Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, No. 2 man at the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), in Mexico City on Sept. 28, 1994.
Altamirano said he told investigators on Nov. 16, 1994, that he did not know Rodriguez.

Raul Salinas de Gortari, the brother of former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari, has been jailed and charged with masterminding the murder. The attorney general's office, which is handling the murder probe, refused to comment.

Reforma said Rodriguez mentioned Altamirano's name twice to prosecutors in connection with the murder. The newspaper based its report on a copy of Rodriguez's testimony in April that Reforma said it received on Tuesday.
Reforma said Raul Salinas used Rodriguez's testimony to defend himself in court, saying the testimony called into doubt government claims Raul Salinas plotted the murder alone.

"(The testimony) talks of those who could possibly benefit from the murder, and (Rodriguez) always mentions that the benefits would be for the next administration, not the administration of Carlos Salinas de Gortari," Salinas said during court testimony in May.
